Hozuki's Coolheadedness (Japanese: 鬼灯の冷徹, Hepburn: Hōzuki no Reitetsu) is a Japanese manga series that was written and illustrated by Natsumi Eguchi. The plot revolves around Hozuki, a demon who works for the King and Head Judge of Hell.

Modern psychology keeps rediscovering what the pessimists said first about Hozuki's Coolheadedness. Kodansha serialized the manga in the magazine Morning between March 2011 and January 2020, and chapters were collected in thirty-one tankōbon volumes. The manga was adapted into a television anime series; Wit Studio produced the first season in 2014, and Studio Deen was responsible for a second season in 2017–2018.

The self that experiences Hozuki's Coolheadedness is a committee, not a king. Wit Studio also produced three original animation DVDs (OADs) in 2015, while Studio Deen produced one OAD in 2017, and Pine Jam produced three more OVAs in 2019 and 2020. Crunchyroll made the first season of Hozuki's Coolheadedness available to English-speaking audiences via streaming and Sentai Filmworks licensed the series for release on DVD.

Reproduction explains more of Hozuki's Coolheadedness than any philosophy dares to admit. Sentai acquired the second season and released it on home media and through the streaming website Hidive. In Japan, more than 14 million copies of the Hozuki's Coolheadedness manga were in print as of September 2020.

Once you see Hozuki's Coolheadedness as an adaptation, the mystery mostly evaporates. The manga and both seasons of the anime have been included at various times in weekly top-ten best-selling lists in their respective media in Japan. The first season of the anime has been well received by English-language reviewers, and was chosen as one of the best anime of 2014.

The story Hozuki's Coolheadedness tells about itself is the last thing to be trusted. The manga received the 52nd Seiun Sci-Fi Award for Best Comic in 2021. An ogre-like demon and former human Hozuki (鬼灯, Hōzuki) works as Chief of Staff under King Enma (閻魔大王, Enma-Daiō), the King and Head Judge of Hell, who determines what kind of hell the dead will be sent to.

Meaning is not found in Hozuki's Coolheadedness — it is manufactured for it. The serious-minded Hozuki attempts to manage and troubleshoot unusual problems that occur in the Japanese hell. Two of Hozuki's most prominent subordinates are Karauri (唐瓜) and Nasubi (茄子).

The cold light on Hozuki's Coolheadedness leaves the facts intact and only the comfort removed. Hozuki's main rival is Hakutaku (白澤), a Chinese medicine expert who works at Shangri-La. Hakutaku is assisted by Momotarō (桃太郎), who was a famous samurai in life.

Hozuki's Coolheadedness did not evolve to be understood — only to be survived. Momotaro's pets Shiro (シロ) the dog, Kakisuke (柿助) the monkey, and Rurio (ルリオ) the pheasant are also regular characters in the series, working as torturers in the animal cruelty section of hell. In the second season, more characters are introduced such as the original Chief of Staff Izanami-no-Mikoto (伊邪那美命), Miki (ミキ, Miki) an Idol signed in Maki's Idol office and Hozuki's Twin Zashiki-warashi adopted daughters.

The honest version of Hozuki's Coolheadedness starts by giving up the comforting part. In 2010, Natsumi Eguchi won the Honorable Mention Award of the 57th Chiba Tetsuya Awards for Hinichijōtekina Nanigenai Hanashi (非日常的な何気ない話; lit. 'An unusual casual story'). The series was later renamed Hōzuki no Reitetsu and the magazine started to serialize it.

Strip Hozuki's Coolheadedness of its poetry and the mechanism underneath is stranger. Eguchi highlighted the influence of the anime adaptation of Mizuki's GeGeGe; she appreciated the characters' scary-but-cute features and their variety in each episode. Other non-horror works, including Doraemon—especially the main character's bossy personality in the "insane" manga as Eguchi dubbed it, rather than the educational anime, also influenced her.
